setup.title.note: Setup page and document title, shared by all three wizard steps.

setup.steps.label.note: Accessible name of the ordered three-step wizard progress list.

setup.steps.signin.note: First wizard step name, not a button to start a second sign-in.

setup.steps.done.note: Third wizard step name, before the user finishes setup.

setup.signin.title.note: Heading for the first setup step.

setup.signin.body.text: The app uses the Microsoft account Windows is signed in with. If Windows uses a local account, sign in on the Microsoft page that opens.
setup.signin.body.note: F24 first-account explanation. Do not promise a choice of account or isolation from the Windows Microsoft account.

setup.signin.privacy.text: Your password stays on the Microsoft page. The app keeps the sign-in in its own Edge profile.
setup.signin.privacy.note: Explains where credentials are entered, without claiming the profile prevents implicit Windows sign-in.

setup.legacy.title.note: Heading for the optional import of an install.ps1 setup.

setup.legacy.body.text: You can use its accounts and settings. Both installs will share the same browser data.
setup.legacy.body.note: Legacy-install import explanation. Sharing browser profiles also shares the run lock.

setup.legacy.import.text: Use the accounts from your earlier install
setup.legacy.import.note: Button calls import_legacy_install, which imports existing profiles and settings.

setup.legacy.imported.note: Success after importing the legacy install. Does not say a run has happened.

setup.schedule.mode.note: Label of the segmented automatic, fixed time and manual control.

setup.schedule.manual.note: Manual schedule mode option, disables the app's Windows task.

setup.schedule.automatic_body.text: Checks {checks} times a day in this window. A run starts only when enough points are open or a quest step is unlocked.
setup.schedule.automatic_body.note: Automatic mode explanation. checks is formatted from schedule.checks; this field is not editable in the wizard.

setup.schedule.fixed_body.text: Checks once at this time, then runs if anything is open. If the page cannot be read, the run goes ahead.
setup.schedule.fixed_body.note: Fixed-time mode semantics with threshold one and unreadable fallback, per section 5.

setup.schedule.manual_body.text: Nothing runs on a schedule. Choose Run now on Overview whenever you want.
setup.schedule.manual_body.note: Manual mode explanation, names the Overview action.

setup.schedule.window.note: Label for the shared timeRange control, using local 24-hour times.

setup.schedule.time.note: Label for the shared fixed-time input, in local time.

setup.schedule.days_toggle.note: Disclosure summary for wizard weekdays, collapsed initially.

setup.schedule.days.note: Accessible group label for the weekday picker.

setup.schedule.independent.text: Windows runs the schedule even when this app is closed. Your PC needs to be on and you need to be signed in.
setup.schedule.independent.note: Explains the interactive Windows Task Scheduler behavior without promising wake from sleep.

setup.schedule.legacy_notice.text: An older daily task is still on this PC. Replace it with the app's schedule, or keep both.
setup.schedule.legacy_notice.note: Section 5.6 notice for the installer's task named rewards-farmer, never the operator's separate task.

setup.schedule.replace.note: Explicit choice calls replace_legacy_task. Never delete the legacy task without this choice.

setup.schedule.keep.note: Explicit choice leaves the older task untouched.

setup.schedule.kept.text: Both schedules stay. Only one run can use the browser data at a time.
setup.schedule.kept.note: After Keep both, explains shared locking without promising that duplicate schedules have no cost.

setup.schedule.replaced.text: The app's schedule replaced the older task
setup.schedule.replaced.note: Success after replace_legacy_task returns, past tense because replacement already happened.

setup.schedule.legacy_choose.text: Choose what happens to the older task first
setup.schedule.legacy_choose.note: Visible disabled-button reason until Replace it or Keep both is chosen.

setup.done.title.note: Heading for the final wizard step, not a claim that a run already finished.

forms.one: Automatic, {checks} check a day between {start} and {end}
forms.other: Automatic, {checks} checks a day between {start} and {end}

setup.summary.automatic.note: Final schedule review. checks is a numeric plural driver formatted by i18n; start and end are region-formatted times. A check is not a promise that a run starts.

setup.summary.fixed.note: Final fixed schedule review. time is already region-formatted. The next line names the selected weekdays or says Every day, so do not repeat a day qualifier here.

setup.summary.every_day.note: Final automatic or fixed schedule review when all seven weekdays are selected. A smaller selection uses the localized weekday list; manual mode has no days line.

setup.done.autostart.note: Switch for app.autostart, on by default in the wizard.

setup.done.autostart_body.text: Keep the app in the tray for status and notifications. Your schedule works without it.
setup.done.autostart_body.note: Description of app autostart, separate from the scheduled farmer.

setup.done.first_run.note: Optional first-run switch, on by default under F46. The user can turn it off; no run starts until Finish and run now is clicked.

setup.done.first_run_body.text: Edge opens and does the daily tasks. You can watch progress on Live run.
setup.done.first_run_body.note: Explains the real effect of opting into the first run.

setup.done.finish.note: Primary button calls complete_setup without starting a run. The tray startup choice was saved in step two and is not written again.

setup.done.finish_run.note: Primary button when the first-run switch is on; saves setup and calls start_run.

setup.done.finished.note: Success state after complete_setup returns, retained if the optional run fails.

setup.done.open_overview.note: Recovery action after setup succeeds but the optional first run fails.

setup.done.retry_run.note: Retries start_run only, not already completed setup.

setup.load.title.note: Friendly empty-state heading for a bridge fetch failure.

setup.recovery.title.note: Inline setup error recovery heading, Settings navigation is hidden during setup.

setup.recovery.body.text: Try again, or export diagnostics here if it keeps happening. You do not need to leave setup.
setup.recovery.body.note: Explains the inline diagnostics action for failed sign-in, task replacement, loading and final setup errors.

setup.recovery.export.note: Calls export_diagnostics and opens the native save picker, never opens Settings or a web page.

setup.recovery.exported.note: Success after the diagnostics save picker returns a path. path is isolated by i18n, never inserted as HTML.

setup.recovery.choose_edge.note: Calls pick_path with kind edge, then saves advanced.edge_path only after a non-null selection.

setup.recovery.edge_help.text: Choose msedge.exe on this PC, then try signing in again.
setup.recovery.edge_help.note: Setup-local recovery for Edge or driver errors, does not direct the user to the hidden Settings screen.

setup.recovery.edge_saved.text: Edge location saved. Try signing in again.
setup.recovery.edge_saved.note: Confirmation after save_settings accepts advanced.edge_path. Does not claim sign-in succeeded.

setup.recovery.reset_driver.note: Explicit action clears advanced.driver_path so Selenium can download the matching driver on the next sign-in.

setup.recovery.driver_help.text: Let the app download the driver that matches Edge. This removes any custom driver location.
setup.recovery.driver_help.note: Visible consequence before the user resets a missing or mismatched driver path.

setup.recovery.driver_reset.text: Custom driver location removed. Try signing in again.
setup.recovery.driver_reset.note: Confirmation after saving advanced.driver_path as empty, not a claim that a download or sign-in completed.
